dedupe_keys.name: remediation of liquefaction effects for an embankment using soil cement walls

description: Remediation of Liquefaction Effects for an Embankment using Soil-cement Walls is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "experimental", published or maintained by Ross Boulanger, University of California Davis (ucdavis.edu). This data report describes the model construction procedure and presents results for a centrifuge test of an embankment on a liquefiable foundation layer treated with soil-cement walls and subjected to seismic loads. The centrifuge experiment was carried out on the 9-m radius centrifuge at the Center for Geotechnical Modeling at UC Davis. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "experimental" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/DS28686. Keywords: Liquefaction, embankment, remediation, soil-cement, centrifuge. Published 2018-05-10. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated in the DesignSafe listing (publication licences offered are CC BY 4.0, ODC-By, CC0 and GPL; project page not read). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
